newsitem.title: JAPAN: Some Japan banks to boost capital in 97/98-analyst.
newsitem.headline: Some Japan banks to boost capital in 97/98-analyst.

text.p: Some Japanese banks, faced with pressure to build up stronger capital positions, are likely to issue preferred stock and to take out subordinated loans in the current business year, according to a report by ING Baring Securities (Japan) Ltd.

Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd, Asahi Bank Ltd, Sanwa Bank Ltd and Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co Ltd are expected to take steps to boost their capital adequacy ratios to a more stable level of 10 percent, the report by financial analyst James Fiorillo said.

Under capital adequacy requirements set by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), Japanese banks operating internationally need to have capital equivalent to a minimum of 8.0 percent of risk-weighted assets.
Fiorillo said the banks are expected to try to boost their capital to met stricter BIS capital adequacy requirements from the end of 1997/98.

"By April 1998 Japanese banks will have more pressure on them to build up their capital positions as required capital will depend on the amount of market risk they bear according to the second-stage guidelines (set by the BIS) to go into effect at that time," he said in his report.

Those second-stage guidelines mean that Japanese banks operating internationally must take into account market risks such as foreign exchange transactions and swaps when calculating their capital adequacy ratios.
"In response Japanese banks are likely to come to the market with preferred share issuances and to secure subordinated loans this year to the tune of at least 800 billion yen," Fiorillo said.

He also said the stricter BIS requirements and an increasingly competitive environment were likely to force some banks to take a second look at whether they want to continue operating internationally.
